risks.title: Government Policy Dependence
risks.score_rationale: Federal or state policies could be enacted that restrict the availability of and increase the costs associated with fuels or generation technologies such as natural gas or nuclear power that enable Duke Energy to reduce its carbon emissions. (Item 1A)

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy is subject to regulation by FERC and state utility regulatory agencies which have jurisdiction over rates and investment recovery. Regulatory decisions can materially impact operating results. (Item 1A, Item 4)

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: Increased competition in the energy sector may impact Duke Energy's operating results and market share across its service territories. (Item 1A)

risks.title: Environmental and Climate Risks
risks.score_rationale: Environmental regulations can increase operating costs. Duke Energy must manage coal-fired facility retirements, replacement generation availability, and comply with emission standards. (Item 1A, Item 7)

risks.title: Technology Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The availability and deployment of generation and grid technologies can impact Duke Energy's ability to achieve modernization and carbon reduction objectives. (Item 1A)

risks.title: Nuclear Operations Risk
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy operates multiple nuclear facilities including McGuire, Oconee, Catawba, Robinson, Brunswick and Harris. Nuclear liability is capped by the Price-Anderson Act at approximately $16.3 billion. Uninsured losses could materially impact operations. (Item 5)

risks.title: Business Strategy Implementation
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy's future results depend on successfully implementing its business strategy to provide reliable energy while maintaining low costs and balancing modernization with carbon reduction objectives amid regulatory uncertainties. (Item 1A)
